limitations: ApoMarioHighscore and its required public methods do not yet exist, so their enforcement-point anchors are prospective and have null file/line values.
The exact authoritative human-name input and whether replay, editor, and AI runs qualify for the board could not be established from the inspected sources.

The exact level/server serialization schema and all allocations inside ApoMarioLevelIO were not fully inspected; the context therefore treats the ApoIO read boundary as the resolved source and records validation needs at the highscore/run-end boundary.

nodes.label: Persisted highscore records: player name, score, survival time
Actual completed-run score and elapsed survival time
Player name shown in the highscore entry
Local highscore store to in-memory records and menu display
nodes.sink: ApoMarioHighscore record lists, sorting, and the dedicated highscore panel display.
nodes.source: ApoMarioHighscore(Path) reading the local store during initialization or persistence reload.
nodes.untrusted_input: The file identified by the constructor Path; the desktop user can edit, truncate, replace, or supply malformed highscore records.

nodes.label: Finished ApoMario level state to a persisted run
nodes.source: The mutable ApoMarioLevel and ApoMarioPlayer objects at the win/loss transition; scoring is finalized in setAnalysis(boolean).
nodes.untrusted_input: In-game values that can be locally tampered with, including player points, player/team name, countdown time, replay/editor state, or level content loaded from files/server content.

nodes.label: Shared level content to live level objects
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevel and its player/scoring state, later consumed by run-end recording.
nodes.source: ApoIO.readLevel(boolean,String) opens either a local FileInputStream or a URL stream and passes decoded bytes to the level reader.
nodes.untrusted_input: Content obtained from a shared level server or a user-selected level file.

nodes.label: ApoMario’s score is mutable on each player and is incremented during setAnalysis(boolean), while the result panel reads the player’s points; the highscore entry must preserve the integrity and authenticity of that finalized value.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature requires recording the real score when the run ends, not a stale or recomputed display value.
nodes.verification: Create a deterministic level/player fixture, invoke the run-end path for both win and loss, and assert the stored score equals the post-setAnalysis player score.

nodes.label: ApoMario exposes the remaining countdown through getTime() and computes passed time as randomLevel.getTime() minus the remaining time; the recorded survival time must preserve elapsed-time integrity and be rendered as mm:ss.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature explicitly requires survival time at run completion.
nodes.verification: Use a level with known initial and remaining time, record the run, and assert the stored integer and rendered representation match the expected elapsed seconds and mm:ss formatting.

nodes.label: ApoIcarus keeps parallel points, time, and names lists and sorts display rows by descending points while rendering name and time together; ApoMario should preserve row alignment while adapting the storage layer.
nodes.task_relevance: The requested board sorts names by points and displays name, score, and survival time as one record.
nodes.verification: Insert records with scores in non-descending order and assert names, scores, and times are returned in matching descending-score row order.

nodes.failure_behavior: Do not carry over donor URL behavior; use the supplied local Path and reject/fall back on malformed local data.
nodes.label: The donor loader clears its lists and parses every incoming line as an integer or name without bounds or record-shape validation, and the donor save/load methods perform URL network I/O; copying this behavior into ApoMario would expose the new feature to malformed input and an out-of-scope network dependency.
nodes.task_relevance: ApoIcarus is the requested donor, but the target requirement is a local Path store and the fixed model does not assume a web endpoint.
nodes.verification: Review the adapted implementation for URL/URLConnection usage and fuzz the local store parser with malformed and oversized records.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject malformed records and bounded-overflow records; fall back to an empty in-memory board without crashing the game.
nodes.label: A Path-backed highscore loader that accepts arbitrary lines or counts can throw numeric parsing exceptions, allocate excessive records, or create inconsistent parallel lists when the local store is malformed.
nodes.task_relevance: The required constructor and persistence API introduce a new local-file decoding boundary.
nodes.verification: Provide empty, truncated, nonnumeric, oversized, and very large-count store files; assert construction completes, no uncaught exception occurs, and only valid bounded records are exposed.

nodes.failure_behavior: Record only after the final score adjustment and terminal outcome are established; if required player/time state is unavailable or invalid, skip the entry and leave the existing board unchanged.
nodes.label: If recordRunEnd reads a mutable or tampered level before scoring is finalized, a user can forge the persisted score, name, or survival time; replay/editor/server-derived state can also be recorded as if it were a normal completed run.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature requires the running game itself to record the actual finished run at both clearing and losing.
nodes.verification: Exercise both bWin values, repeated setAnalysis calls, replay/editor modes, null/empty player collections, and unavailable random-level timing; assert exactly one valid entry only for the intended completed run.

nodes.failure_behavior: Normalize and bound names at storeRun; replace null/invalid names with a fixed fallback or reject the run, and render only the bounded value.
nodes.label: A user-controlled name copied directly into the board can spoof another player, corrupt row layout, or cause excessive rendering work when displayed without a bounded representation.
nodes.task_relevance: The board must display the player’s name and persist it across runs.
nodes.verification: Store null, empty, overlong, whitespace, control-character, and look-alike names; assert the documented reject/fallback behavior and bounded rendering.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject invalid records and excessive sizes, then use an empty or last-known-good in-memory board; persistence failure must leave the running game usable.
nodes.label: ApoMarioHighscore(Path) and persistAcrossRuns must decode and encode a bounded, versioned local file format for names, scores, and survival times; malformed records must not enter the returned lists or crash the menu.
nodes.task_relevance: This is required for persistence across runs while crossing the user-editable local-file boundary.
nodes.verification: Round-trip valid records through a new instance; corrupt each field and truncate the file; assert bounded rejection, no crash, and persistence after a second instance.

nodes.failure_behavior: If terminal data cannot be obtained or is invalid, do not persist a fabricated partial record; retain the board and continue to the existing analysis/menu flow.
nodes.label: The run-end integration must call recordRunEnd(ApoMarioLevel) exactly once after the final win/loss score mutation, deriving the intended human player’s actual points, player name, and elapsed seconds from that level, and must not record a new run when the level is merely restarted or a menu transition occurs.
nodes.task_relevance: This enforces the requested real run result for clearing and losing.
nodes.verification: Instrument or spy on the highscore object across win, loss, restart, new-level, replay, and menu paths; assert one call only for each terminal run and verify exact score/name/time values.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject or replace invalid names and invalid score/time ranges; do not mutate the lists when validation fails.
nodes.label: storeRun(int,String) must validate and normalize the player name before inserting it, preserve name/score/time row alignment, and maintain descending score order for getPlayersNames(), getPlayersScores(), and getSurvivalTimes().
nodes.task_relevance: The board must display the player name and sort names by points descending without allowing malformed names to affect the UI.
nodes.verification: Test valid and invalid inputs, duplicate scores, negative values, integer extremes, and repeated insertions; assert atomic rejection and descending aligned rows.

nodes.failure_behavior: If loading fails, show an empty/error-safe board and retain a working back/menu action.
nodes.label: The dedicated ApoMario highscore panel must load the local board, display names, scores, and survival times as mm:ss, and be reachable from the existing menu state without exposing raw unbounded store content.
nodes.task_relevance: This implements the requested dedicated menu view and display behavior.
nodes.verification: Navigate from the menu to the panel with empty, valid, and corrupt stores; assert all fields render, time is mm:ss, scores descend, and back navigation remains available.

nodes.failure_behavior: Fall back to an empty/last-known-good board and continue rendering; never propagate parser exceptions to the game loop.
nodes.label: At the Path-store read operation, parse a strict format with a maximum record count, maximum name length, finite nonnegative score/time bounds, complete rows, and a format/version marker; ignore or reject the entire invalid record set on failure.
nodes.task_relevance: This is the concrete enforcement control for malformed user-editable persistence data.
nodes.verification: Fuzz and property-test the decoder with malformed delimiters, invalid integers, huge counts, long names, truncated rows, and unsupported versions.

nodes.failure_behavior: Skip the entry and continue normal analysis if the level/player/timing snapshot is invalid or the run-end marker was already consumed.
nodes.label: At the run-end call site in setAnalysis(boolean), guard the terminal transition so recording occurs after final score adjustments and only once per run; obtain the selected human player’s points/name and elapsed time from the same level snapshot, and reject unavailable or inconsistent values.
nodes.task_relevance: This binds the persisted record to the actual clearing/losing event instead of a mutable later menu state.
nodes.verification: Use mocks/fixtures to force duplicate terminal calls, null players, invalid time, and score changes before/after analysis; assert one atomic record only after finalization.

nodes.failure_behavior: Return false and leave all lists unchanged for rejected input; return true only after the complete row is accepted and ordered.
nodes.label: At storeRun, trim and bound the name, reject control characters and null/empty values according to a fixed fallback policy, validate score and survival time ranges, and insert the three fields as one immutable row before sorting by numeric score descending.
nodes.task_relevance: This prevents malformed or spoofing-oriented local names and preserves display integrity.
nodes.verification: Assert return values, list immutability on failure, aligned row ordering, and bounded output for adversarial names and integer extremes.

nodes.failure_behavior: On access, serialization, or replacement failure, retain the in-memory board, report failure through the existing safe error path, and keep the menu usable.
nodes.label: At persistAcrossRuns, write a bounded snapshot using a temporary file and replace the configured Path only after successful serialization; do not use the donor’s URL/URLConnection save path.
nodes.task_relevance: This makes persistence local, prevents partial writes from corrupting the board, and honors the required Path store.
nodes.verification: Inject unwritable, missing-parent, full-disk, and interruption scenarios; assert no partial target file is accepted and the in-memory board remains available.

nodes.label: Verify the complete data flow with a temporary Path: store valid rows, persist, construct a second ApoMarioHighscore, and assert names, scores, survival times, descending order, and mm:ss display all survive the reload.
nodes.task_relevance: Covers the primary feature contract and persistence boundary.
nodes.verification: Automated round-trip integration test using a temporary file and representative scores/times/names.

nodes.label: Verify run-end provenance by exercising clear and loss paths with known player points, name, and countdown values, then asserting recordRunEnd produces exactly one matching persisted row and no row for restart/menu-only transitions.
nodes.task_relevance: Covers the authenticity and deduplication requirement for actual finished runs.
nodes.verification: Instrumented integration test over win, loss, duplicate callbacks, restart, replay, editor, and menu flows.

nodes.failure_behavior: Do not guess a name or silently persist an AI/replay/editor result; define and test the policy before integration.
nodes.label: The inspected ApoMario sources do not establish a dedicated human player-name input or a single authoritative policy for which player is recorded in one-player, two-player, replay, editor, and AI modes; the current analysis uses player/team-derived names while the single-player loss text uses the literal human label.
nodes.task_relevance: Implementation must resolve the name source and eligible-run policy before recordRunEnd can satisfy the real-name requirement.
nodes.verification: Document the selected source and mode exclusions, then add tests for human, AI, replay, editor, missing-name, and two-player scenarios.

summary: ApoMario currently derives run results from ApoMarioLevel and ApoMarioPlayer at analysis time, displays names/scores/time, and persists only general properties. ApoIcarus provides a reusable highscore model and sorted panel pattern, but its implementation uses network I/O and unbounded parsing; the ApoMario adaptation should use the required local Path store, validate all decoded records, and record the final level state exactly once at the win/loss transition.
